Test them: P(1) = 3, P(−1) = 15, P(2) = 0. Dividing out leaves x² + x − 5, and x² + x − 5 has discriminant 21, not a perfect square, so its zeros are irrational. So the one rational zero is 2.

problems.explain: A rational zero p/q in lowest terms has p dividing the constant term, −2, and q dividing the leading coefficient, 1. So the candidates are ±1, ±2. Test them: P(1) = −3, P(−1) = −3, P(2) = 0. Dividing out leaves x² + x + 1, and x² + x + 1 has discriminant −3, negative, so no real zeros at all. So the one rational zero is 2.
